Good evening, everyone, and thank you for coming out on a Wednesday. I want to talk about the festival, the money, and the noise complaints, because all three have been in the news this month.

Let me start with the money. Last year the festival sold forty one thousand tickets across four days. That number surprised us. We had planned for thirty thousand, and the extra crowd is the reason the beach road was blocked for six hours on the Saturday. I am sorry about that. It should not have happened, and it will not happen again.

Now, the question everyone keeps asking me. Are tickets getting more expensive? Here is the answer, and I want to be very clear about it. We will not raise ticket prices this year. The early bird price stays at two thousand rupees, and students still get half off with a college ID.

What we are changing is where the money goes. Twelve percent of every ticket now goes to the village panchayat, for waste collection and for the night buses. That is not a donation. It is in the contract, and the contract is public.

Second, the noise. I have read every complaint. Some of them are fair. The main stage will shut down at ten pm, every night, no exceptions, and the silent disco tent will run until midnight with headphones only. We are not moving the festival to a new site. We looked at three alternatives, and none of them had road access for emergency vehicles.

Third, safety. We are doubling the number of trained medics on site, from twenty to forty. There will be free drinking water at every gate. We never charge for water, and we never will.

Some people have told me that the festival only benefits the hotels in Calangute. That is partly true, and I do not want to hide from it. So this year, sixty local food stalls get free space, and the selection is done by the panchayat, not by us.

Let me say something about the rumours. You may have seen a video saying the festival is cancelled. That video is old. It is from the lockdown year. The festival is not cancelled. It starts on the twentieth of December, as planned.

I also want to address the artists. We are not booking any act that has a pending case for violence. That rule is new, and it applies to everyone, including the headliners.

Finally, the volunteers. We need three hundred of them. Volunteers get a free pass, two meals a day, and a certificate. If you are under eighteen, you need a parent's signature. We cannot make an exception to that, even for one day.

So, to sum up. Prices stay the same. The stage closes at ten. Water is free. And the festival is not cancelled. Thank you. I will take questions now.
